title: Vishvamitra takes the boys
hook: the verse that wakes Rama on his first morning away from home is still sung at dawn

segments.voice: Yesterday: Vishvamitra takes the boys, part one. A promise, a plea, and a sage's anger shaking the earth. Did you pause before promising whatever someone wanted? Today, the boys go. Day four hundred ninety-nine.

In many homes and temples in South India, the day starts with a recording of a Sanskrit hymn called the Venkatesha Suprabhatam, a song to wake the Lord at Tirupati. Its very first verse isn't new. It's borrowed, word for word, from the Ramayana. It's what Vishvamitra says to wake Rama on his first morning away from home, sleeping on grass by a river. Before we get there, though, the boys have to leave.
screen: `A HYMN AT DAWN IN SOUTH INDIA.` → `ITS FIRST VERSE IS FROM THE RAMAYANA.` → `RAMA'S FIRST MORNING AWAY.`

segments.voice: Vasishtha, the royal priest, speaks to the frightened king. You've given your word, he says. Breaking it would undo all your merit. And look who's asking. Vishvamitra knows every divine weapon there is. Rama will be safer with him than anywhere. Dasharatha listens, and yields. He calls for Rama, and Lakshmana, who won't be left behind, and blesses them. The boys walk out after the sage, bows in hand, quivers on their backs, and the text says a soft breeze blew and flowers fell from the sky. After a day's walk, on the south bank of the Sarayu, Vishvamitra stops and teaches Rama two mantras, bala and atibala, strength and great strength. With these, he says, you won't feel hunger or thirst or tiredness, and no one will match you, awake or asleep. That night, the princes sleep on grass, like ordinary travelers. And at dawn, the sage wakes them: kausalya supraja rama purva sandhya pravartate, uttishtha narashardula kartavyam daivam ahnikam. Rama, fortunate son of Kausalya, the morning twilight is here. Rise, tiger among men, the day's sacred duties are waiting. The boys rise, bathe, say their prayers, and walk on, to a hermitage where, the sage tells them, Shiva once burned Kama, the god of desire, to ash. The boys have left their father's house. Their teacher's world has begun.
screen: `VASISHTHA: KEEP YOUR WORD.` · `THE BOYS WALK OUT, FLOWERS FALL.` · `BALA AND ATIBALA BY THE RIVER.` · `A SAGE WAKES THEM AT DAWN.` · then, large: `KAUSALYĀ SUPRAJĀ RĀMA PŪRVĀ SANDHYĀ PRAVARTATE.`

segments.voice: Sit as if it's very early, the light just starting. Let the breath be slow, like someone waking. Imagine a kind voice saying your name, the way Vishvamitra said Rama's: not rushing you, just letting you know the day has come. On each breath in, rise a little. On each breath out, settle into the day you actually have. The bell holds the time.
Atibala, great strength, one of the two mantras Vishvamitra teaches Rama. Persuaded by Vasishtha, Dasharatha lets Rama and Lakshmana go, and the sage teaches them, and wakes them, on the road.
Your line: rise, tiger among men. Tomorrow morning, wake someone, or yourself, the way the sage did: by name, gently, with the day's good work waiting. Day four hundred ninety-nine.

howItsDone: The Venkatesha Suprabhatam, sung at dawn at the Tirumala temple and played in many homes, opens with Vishvamitra's verse from the Bala Kanda waking Rama.

fork.setup: you're Vasishtha. the king won't send his son with the sage. what do you advise?
options: keep your word; the boy will be safe with this sage.
ask the sage to choose another prince.
fork.reveal: Vasishtha reminds him a broken promise undoes merit, and that Vishvamitra knows every divine weapon. Dasharatha lets the boys go.

original.note: Sanskrit atibalā: great strength. with balā, strength, the two mantras Vishvamitra teaches Rama.

trapdoor: what you thought: the dawn hymn was written for the temple.
what it means: its opening verse is Vishvamitra's wake-up call to Rama, from the Bala Kanda.
what a scholar hears: Bala Kanda 23.2 opens the Venkatesha Suprabhatam; bala and atibala, given in sarga 22, are called daughters of Brahma in the text.

sources.quoted: kausalyā suprajā rāma pūrvā sandhyā pravartate

sources.ref: Valmiki Ramayana, Bala Kanda 21–22 (Vasishtha's counsel; departure; bala and atibala)

notes: The full verse (uttishtha narashardula kartavyam daivam ahnikam) is spoken in transliteration; only the first half is listed as quoted. Confirm transliteration.
'Bala and atibala as daughters of Brahma' in the trapdoor: confirm (sarga 22).
Day's walk distance: the text gives a yojana and a half; the script says 'a day's walk'.
